title: rebuilt starworld as a visual roguelike - relaunching (again)
author: Diligent-Garage1773
selftext:
starworld is a sci-fi roguelike where you run procedurally generated zones, fight turn-based battles, and collect gear. everything has ai-generated pixel art.

what's in the game:

journey mode: enter a zone, fight through rooms, find vendors and treasure, beat the boss, extract with your loot

pvp ladder: async battles against other players' heroes using their actual builds

core fusion: burn excess crafting materials to generate new gear

talent trees and ability loadouts that actually matter in combat

relaunching on ios first, android after.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/starworld-ai/id6743031331

comments.author: fisj
comments.body:
Please follow the following when making a commercial post about your game. Right now this is a fire and forget post advertising to the community with nothing to offer.

1. **You may Promote your Commercial Game, BUT ...**
   1. Promoting your game is still fine, HOWEVER, you must discuss your game within the context of how it was developed using AI. Share with the community and give something for the community to talk about.
   2. If its a fire and forget video, or low effort chatGPT bullet list, it may be flagged as spam by mods.
   3. Generally, you're cooked if you're relying on promotion to other devs. This is the place to get help to develop and learn.
   4. Don't forget to apply the "Commercial Self Promotion" tag/flair!

replies.author: Diligent-Garage1773
replies.body: Sure happy to add more context: the relaunch was developed over this past weekend using SDD / IDD (whatever you prefer to call the new spec driven development paradigm) using opensource software I have been working on to sort of ‘level up’ vibe coding to be a bit more capable of enterprise grade production (happy to share this software as well if there is interest). The net of things as that it integrates with copilot which becomes the development engine you feed feature specs to… two days later: relaunch!

replies.author: fisj
replies.body: Thank you for elaborating. This actually an area a lot of others here are struggling with. There's an explosion of capability in agent and ai assisted coding, people try it and hit walls. Insight on workflows in a production game development pipeline is rare right now, and if you have thoughts I'm sure the community would be grateful.
